steps.title: Requirements
steps.output: Functional list, non-functional list, out of scope
steps.guide: The most valuable time in the interview: build the right thing before building the thing right. Functional: the 3–5 things a user can do, written as verbs. Non-functional: scale, latency, availability, consistency, durability; ask which matters most. Out of scope: say what you're skipping. End by reading the list back: "Does this match what you had in mind?"

steps.title: Estimates
steps.output: Users, QPS, storage: only the numbers that change a decision
steps.guide: Napkin math, but only as far as it changes a decision. "About 1,000 bookings per second at peak, so one database can handle writes" is useful; storage to three digits is not. If the numbers don't change anything, say so and move on.

steps.title: API
steps.guide: Write each endpoint with its key inputs and outputs. It pins down what the system actually does before you draw boxes. Mention pagination, idempotency keys for anything that charges money, and REST vs. GraphQL vs. gRPC only if it matters.

steps.title: Data model
steps.output: Main entities, keys, and which store holds them
steps.guide: List the main entities, their keys and the relationships between them. Then pick a store for each and give one reason: "Bookings go in a relational database because I need transactions to prevent double booking."

steps.title: High-level design
steps.guide: Draw the simplest system that satisfies every functional requirement (Diagram tab): clients, load balancer, services, databases, caches, queues. Then trace one request through it out loud. If a requirement has no box that serves it, you've found a gap. Keep it simple on purpose; scaling comes next.

steps.title: Deep dives
steps.guide: This is where you earn the grade. Pick the 2–3 hardest parts of this problem, say why they're hard, and design them properly: where correctness matters most, the hottest path at scale, the part most likely to fail. Propose them yourself.

steps.title: Wrap-up
steps.output: Bottlenecks, failure modes, what you'd do next
steps.guide: Name the biggest remaining bottleneck, one or two failure modes and how you'd detect them, and what you'd build next. Ending on a clear summary leaves a strong last impression.

checklist: Requirements written: functional, non-functional, out of scope. Read back and confirmed.
Estimates done only where they change a decision.
API sketched, with idempotency keys on anything that moves money.
Data model with a store chosen for each entity, and a reason.
High-level diagram covers every functional requirement; one request traced end to end.
Deep dives started by minute 25, and I proposed them.
Every major choice stated with an alternative and a reason.
At least two failure modes raised, with how I'd detect them.
Closed with the biggest remaining risk and the next step.
